layout_sources: https://github.com/ThibaultLanternier/bank-data-parser/pull/8 and issue #5 (October 2026: "support new boursobank csv export format" - French headers "Date Opération", "Date Valeur", Libellé, "Libellé Suggéré", Catégorie, "Catégorie Parente", Solde, Commentaire, "Numéro Compte", "Libellé Compte", Solde, Pointage; the first Solde is the amount, the second the balance; the tests show the rows, read as utf-8-sig)

The same repository's older format (to mid-2026): dateOp;dateVal;label;category;categoryParent;supplierFound;amount;comment;accountNum;accountLabel;accountbalance, ISO dates, "-1 104,95", balance "266.19"
https://github.com/reubano/csv2ofx/blob/master/csv2ofx/mappings/boursorama.py (2020: semicolon, header, amount with spaces removed and comma swapped, accountbalance)
notes: boursobank.com account "Exporter en format CSV", the layout from October 2026: UTF-8 with BOM, semicolon-separated, header cells quoted only when they hold a space, text values quoted, ISO dates, the amount column headed "Solde" (sic) with a space as the thousands mark and a comma decimal ("-1 140,00"), the account balance in a second "Solde" column with a point decimal ("1763.61"), Pointage Non/Oui. Newest first. LF line ends assumed; whether the thousands space is a plain or a no-break space is not confirmed (plain here). No currency is written. Closing = the newest line's balance; opening = the oldest line's balance minus its amount.
